title: Pauri 40, meaning: hear the bliss
hook: hear the song of bliss, fortunate ones; all longings are fulfilled (Anand 40)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sound of pauri forty, and your line, anad sunahu. Can you still say the first line? Anad sunahu, vaddabhaageeho, sagal manorath poore. Today, what it means. Day four hundred one.

Think of a list you keep, on paper or in your head, of things you want. A job. A test result. A phone call from someone. A child who sleeps through the night. Most of us carry a long one, and it gets longer the moment anything on it is crossed off. Now imagine hearing someone call out across a crowded hall: listen, you lucky ones, every one of those longings is met. That's how the last pauri of the Anand begins. Today: pauri forty, the meaning.
screen: `THE LIST OF THINGS YOU WANT.` → `IT GROWS AS YOU CROSS THINGS OFF.` → `LISTEN, LUCKY ONES: ALL LONGINGS MET.`

segments.voice: Here's the first line, in paraphrase. Anad sunahu: hear the bliss. Vaddabhaageeho: you of great fortune. Sagal manorath poore: all longings are fulfilled. Then the pauri says how. The Supreme Lord has been found, and every anxiety is gone. Pain, sickness and suffering leave, it says, by hearing the true bani. The saints and friends are delighted, because they've come to know it through the perfect Guru. Then a line that echoes a pauri we heard nine days ago. Back in pauri twenty-four, unripe were the speakers and unripe the hearers. Here, at the end, it flips: pure are those who hear, holy are those who speak, and the True Guru fills everything. The Anand closes with Nanak's prayer, at the Guru's feet, and a sound: the unstruck music, anahad, playing on and on, like trumpets nobody is blowing. So what does every longing met mean? Not that the list gets checked off. People who sing this pauri still have bills, illnesses and phone calls that don't come. The pauri says the longings are fulfilled because the One they were all reaching for has been found. The list was a long way of wanting one thing. Many Sikhs hear this as the reason the Anand is sung at the end of everything: whatever the occasion was about, the song ends where all the longings end. Every longing met.
screen: `HEAR THE BLISS, YOU FORTUNATE ONES.` · `THE LORD FOUND, EVERY ANXIETY GONE.` · `PURE ARE THE HEARERS, HOLY THE SPEAKERS.` · `THE UNSTRUCK MUSIC PLAYS ON.` · then, large: `EVERY LONGING MET.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to the last pauri whole. If you can find a recording of the six pauris, play the final one, from anad sunahu to the end, and just let it pass through you. If you can't, sit with the first line: anad sunahu vaddabhaageeho sagal manorath poore. Bring one longing from your list to mind, and set it gently beside the line. Not to cancel it. Just to see it in that light. Then breathe. The bell holds the time.
Pauri forty. The last pauri of the Anand: hear the bliss, fortunate ones, all longings are fulfilled; pure are the hearers, holy the speakers; the unstruck music plays.
Your line: every longing met. Today, when you catch yourself adding to the list, pause, and ask what you're really reaching for underneath it. Day four hundred one.

howItsDone: The fortieth pauri is sung with the first five at the close of Sikh services and ceremonies, and is the last pauri of the full Anand Sahib that many Sikhs recite each morning.

myth: pauri forty says the hearers and speakers are pure
the reverse of pauri 24, where both were unripe.
every longing met means everything on your list gets checked off
the pauri says longings are fulfilled because the One they reached for is found.
it ends with the unstruck music, anahad, playing on.

fork.setup: pauri 24 said unripe are the speakers and unripe the hearers. what does pauri 40 say about them?
options: pure are the hearers, holy are the speakers.
fork.reveal: at the end of the Anand it flips: hearing the true bani, the hearers and speakers are made pure.

original.note: Gurmukhi: manorath, a longing, a heart's wish; in pauri 40, sagal manorath poore: all longings fulfilled.

trapdoor: what you thought: every longing met means God gives you everything you want.
what it means: the longings are fulfilled because the One they were all reaching for has been found.

what a scholar hears: the final pauri answers pauri 24 almost word for word, unripe speakers and hearers becoming pure ones, and closes on anahad, the unstruck sound, a term with a long history in Indian devotional and yogic language.

notes: Pauri 40 paraphrased line by line: hear the bliss, fortunate ones, all longings fulfilled; the Supreme Lord found, anxieties (visoore) gone; pain, illness and suffering leave hearing the true bani; saints and friends delighted, knowing it through the perfect Guru; sunate puneet kahate pavit (pure the hearers, holy the speakers); Nanak at the Guru's feet, the unstruck bugles (anahad toore) sound. Confirm glosses.
The link between pauri 24 (kahade kache sunade kache) and pauri 40 (sunate puneet kahate pavit) is the writer's observation; confirm it's fair.
